subject: Routing a task to OpenAI's GPT-5.5 frontier model versus the Claude tiers

cases.scenario: A team needs to author a multi-stage CI pipeline (build matrix, caching, deploy gates) plus a batch of small, well-specified shell/Terraform scripts. Someone proposes 'send it to the strongest model we have' and reaches for the architecture-grade tier by default.
cases.context: Both a GPT frontier tier and the Claude tiers are available. The work is concrete and well-specified, not architecturally novel.
cases.question: Which model should this work be routed to, and why?
expected_flags: The task's dominant axis is concrete CLI/infra implementation, an axis GPT-5 (current GPT-5.5) owns (Terminal-Bench / tool-use lead)
'Use the strongest model' is the wrong primitive — strength is task-shaped, and this axis routes to GPT-5, not the architecture tier
expected_fix_hints: Route the CI/infra/scripting work to GPT-5 because its dominant axis is concrete implementation and CLI/tool-use
Name the axis explicitly before routing rather than defaulting to a habitual 'strongest' choice
absent_signals: Do not claim GPT-5 is universally the best coding model
Do not route purely on aggregate benchmark rank instead of task axis

cases.scenario: A monolith must be re-architected into services, touching ~40 files with cross-cutting dependency changes and a new module boundary design. A teammate wants to route it to GPT-5 because 'GPT-5.5 is #1 on SWE-bench Verified.'
cases.context: The work is architecture-heavy and spans many files with complex resolution. Both frontier tiers are available.
cases.question: Is GPT-5 the right route here, and how should the decision be reasoned?
expected_flags: The dominant axis is broad architecture + complex multi-file resolution, where Claude Opus leads (SWE-bench Pro)
The SWE-bench Verified headline does not generalize — its margin is within noise/contamination caveats and the ranking flips on multi-file resolution
expected_fix_hints: Route the re-architecture to Claude Opus, not GPT-5
Reason from the task's dominant axis, treating a single verified-bench lead as non-decisive for architecture work
absent_signals: Do not route the cross-system re-architecture to GPT-5 on the strength of a verified-bench score
Do not treat 'highest verified score' as 'route all coding here'

cases.scenario: A teammate routing rule is 'always pick whichever model has the cheaper per-token output price.' They route everything away from GPT-5 because its $30 output is higher than the Claude Opus $25, on a workspace that pays a flat subscription, including a long-context (>272K token) analysis job.
cases.context: Billing is a flat subscription, not per-token API. One job sends >272K input tokens.
cases.question: What is wrong with this routing rule and how should cost actually factor in?
expected_flags: Headline per-token price is the wrong primitive — capability-per-task dominates the routing decision
On a flat subscription the per-token USD is notional, not the billed cost, so it should not drive routing
If per-token cost ever does matter, the >272K-token surcharge (2x in / 1.5x out for the full session) must be accounted for, not just the base rate
expected_fix_hints: Route on task axis and capability; use price only as a tie-breaker on a true per-token billing basis
Account for the long-context surcharge when costing the >272K job, rather than comparing base rates
absent_signals: Do not endorse routing by headline per-token price
Do not treat notional subscription per-token USD as the billed cost

cases.scenario: An auth-middleware diff needs a careful analytical code review and a security pass before merge. The team asks which model to assign.
cases.context: The work is analytical diff-reading and threat-surface review, not implementation or architecture.
cases.question: Which model fits this review, and on what basis?
expected_flags: Analytical diff review + security review is an axis GPT-5 is strong on (analytical diff-reading, threat-surface work)
The route follows the axis, not a default-to-strongest habit
expected_fix_hints: Route the analytical/security review to GPT-5, naming the review axis as the reason
Keep architecture-grade reasoning on Opus only if the diff turns out to require broad multi-file redesign
absent_signals: Do not claim only one model can review code
Do not over-weight a single benchmark over the task's actual review axis

cases.scenario: An agent confidently routes a job citing 'GPT-5's context window is exactly 1.05M and output is $30' from memory, without checking the live provider docs, even though the model line iterates point releases frequently.
cases.context: The provider iterates GPT-5 generations, context windows, and pricing fast; the cited numbers may be stale.
cases.question: What should the agent do before relying on those capability and pricing facts?
expected_flags: Capability and pricing facts for the GPT-5 line go stale fast and must be re-verified against live provider docs before being relied on
A stale context-window or pricing number can flip the routing decision
expected_fix_hints: Re-check the current GPT-5 generation, context window, and pricing against the provider's live documentation before routing on a specific number
Treat the skill's quoted numbers as a dated snapshot, not a live source
absent_signals: Do not present remembered version/pricing numbers as currently authoritative
Do not route on an unverified specific figure

cases.scenario: A user asks: 'Resume my last Codex session non-interactively and keep going on the migration — also, while you're at it, which of my local skills handles webhook tasks?'
cases.context: The request is about running a CLI harness session and about request-time dispatch among local skills — neither is a GPT-vs-Claude model-routing decision.
cases.question: How should the agent scope this request?
expected_flags: Resuming a Codex session is a harness operation owned by the Codex skill, not a GPT-vs-Claude model-routing decision
Choosing which local skill handles webhook tasks is request-time dispatch owned by the skill-router, a different layer
expected_fix_hints: Route the Codex session-resume to the Codex harness skill
Route the local-skill dispatch question to the skill-router skill
absent_signals: Do not answer the Codex-resume request as if it were a model-routing decision
Do not treat local-skill dispatch as within this skill's scope
